student_passage:
The first case (0) WAS designed for a laboratory, not for a week on a research vessel. To fit the available storage space, the crew removed internal divisions to (1) ____ an extent that the instruments could move between compartments. The problem was not (2) ____ because the foam lining had become thinner, but because the case no longer held each item in a fixed position.

The equipment technician proposed a removable frame. In (3) ____ of initial objections about its weight, she persuaded the crew to try it. Fitting the frame was by (4) ____ means a routine job: every instrument had to be accessible without lifting out the others. With (5) ____ to the smaller components, she suggested fabric pockets attached to the underside of the lid.

The crew had to decide whether or (6) ____ to retain the old numbering system. They eventually gave each pocket a code of its (7) ____, printed both inside the case and on a separate checklist. A trial run then revealed that two cables could not be coiled into their assigned spaces. The pockets were altered before departure, and the technician demonstrated the packing sequence during the final briefing on (8) ____ the crew had agreed. Once at sea, they would have to pack the case without her help.
filled_passage:
The first case (0) WAS designed for a laboratory, not for a week on a research vessel. To fit the available storage space, the crew removed internal divisions to (1) such an extent that the instruments could move between compartments. The problem was not (2) only because the foam lining had become thinner, but because the case no longer held each item in a fixed position.

The equipment technician proposed a removable frame. In (3) spite of initial objections about its weight, she persuaded the crew to try it. Fitting the frame was by (4) no means a routine job: every instrument had to be accessible without lifting out the others. With (5) regard to the smaller components, she suggested fabric pockets attached to the underside of the lid.

The crew had to decide whether or (6) not to retain the old numbering system. They eventually gave each pocket a code of its (7) own, printed both inside the case and on a separate checklist. A trial run then revealed that two cables could not be coiled into their assigned spaces. The pockets were altered before departure, and the technician demonstrated the packing sequence during the final briefing on (8) which the crew had agreed. Once at sea, they would have to pack the case without her help.
